claims.text: The scheme is for specialist arts institutions or registered charities.

Institutions may apply to both schemes if applicable, but each application will be considered separately.
Individual scholars or students may not apply directly to the Trust.
Awards will run for three years, starting from September 1, 2025.
Eligible organizations must be specialist arts training institutions or registered charities that can demonstrate outstanding quality teaching.
Institutions can make only one application per round.
The applying organization is responsible for selecting recipients, administering funds, and reporting to the Trust.
Non-specialist arts schools are not eligible.
Multi-faculty universities are not eligible.
The Trust aims to support excellent students who lack the financial means to attend high-quality courses from specialist providers.
The scheme is not designed to address access to the Arts for all.
Funds are not available for courses for over-18s.
Funds are not available for degree-level courses.
Organizations can apply for support to cover costs for outstanding students in financial need.
An institution can request funds for more than one type of artistic activity or form of financial support.
Funds can support local, regional, and national arts training for skills building, technique improvement, and specialist provision through weekend, after-school, or summer school programs.
Awards can support the search for new talent and excellence via structured outreach activities.
Funds are expected to cover the full course of training for each scholar, but not the entire cost of putting on a course or funding all students.

Requests for lesser amounts than the maximum will be considered.
